definitions.definition: Concentration, meditation and samādhi together on one object (3.4). Mastery of it gives the light of insight (3.5); it is applied to the stage next after the one mastered (3.6); the three are inner limbs relative to the earlier five and outer relative to the seedless samādhi (3.7-3.8). Most of the powers of the Vibhūti-pāda are stated as following from saṃyama on some object.

name: The powers as obstacles in samādhi (3.37)

names.name: The powers as obstacles in samādhi (3.37)

definitions.definition: The powers arising from saṃyama, beginning with prātibha (3.36), are obstacles (upasarga) for a mind in samādhi and powers (siddhi) for the outgoing mind (3.37). At 3.51 the text adds a warning: when invited by those of high stations the yogin is to feel neither attachment nor pride, for heedlessness would find a gap and stir the afflictions, and then the undesirable would follow again.
